**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

yes that happens if I do this:


```
c = e.connect()

print c.scalar("select 1")

raw_input("ok restrt the DB")

c.close()

```

that's as documented; you are calling "close" on a connection that's been killed, there is no way to avoid a stack trace when you make use of a connection that's been pulled from the other end.  Usually when a connection that's still in use has been killed, you'd be calling execute() or similar upon it in which case it would raise fully.  For close() you at least get to continue as it's emitted only as a log message, since it's a close().

**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

OK, note that you are in fact leaving a connection open in the example above:


    res0 = engine.execute("select 1").fetchone()

since you are only calling fetchone() and not first(), res0 still has an open cursor that will only be closed when you call fetchone() again and no row is returned, or if you call res0.close().
